subject: english-literature
title: Biographical Context
welcome_lead: An author study reads a writer's work alongside their life. Biography is not destiny, but it illuminates the writing.
meta_desc: English Literature: author study, biographical context, recurring themes.
final_note: The life is not the work — but it can light the work.

concepts.def: Reading a text in light of the author's life and experiences.
An author's complete body of work.

An image or idea that appears repeatedly across an author's work.
Foucault's concept of authorship as a discursive role rather than a person.
Roland Barthes's essay arguing meaning resides in the reader, not the author.

walkthroughs.body_html: Knowing Sylvia Plath's depression illuminates Ariel, but reducing the poems to autobiography flattens them. Use biography as one lens among several.
For Foucault, the 'author' is a function of discourse that organises texts. Asking 'who speaks?' is also asking what cultural role the author plays.
Barthes shifts authority from author to reader. The essay is provocative; you don't have to accept it, but you should answer it.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet is any short love poem.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).
